stem: The Stamp Act Congress was historically significant because it...

options.text: Brought nine colonies together in their first joint action against Britain
Declared the colonies independent of Great Britain and its king
options.misconception: Independence came eleven years later, in 1776 — in 1765 the delegates still called themselves loyal subjects petitioning for their rights.

options.text: Created a Continental Army to defend the colonies by force
options.misconception: No army was created in 1765 — the Continental Army came with the Second Continental Congress in 1775, after Lexington and Concord.

options.text: Persuaded Parliament to repeal the Stamp Act in 1766
options.misconception: Parliament repealed the Stamp Act in 1766 under pressure from British merchants as well as colonial protest — the Congress petitioned, but it did not repeal the act itself.

rationales.A: Nine colonies sent delegates to New York in October 1765 — the first time the colonies acted together against Britain. The Congress turned separate colonial grievances into one colonial voice.
rationales.B: No independence was declared in 1765. The delegates petitioned the king as loyal subjects; independence was still eleven years away.
rationales.C: There was no army in 1765. The Continental Army belongs to 1775, after the fighting had already begun.
rationales.D: The Congress had no power to repeal anything. Repeal came from Parliament in 1766, pressed by merchants and by colonial resistance.
rationales.general:
1. Count the colonies. Nine sent delegates to New York — more acting together than ever before.
2. Ask what they produced. One Declaration, speaking for all of them, instead of nine separate petitions.
3. Ask why that mattered. Separate complaints could be ignored one by one; a joint declaration showed London the colonies could act as one.
Remember: unity starts with meeting in the same room.
